dossier.headline: Gulf risk returns as tankers are hit near Hormuz
dossier.summary: Late last week Trump pushed a decision on new Iran strikes into 2027, which eased near-term escalation fears for oil. Over the weekend the picture turned: tankers were struck near the Strait of Hormuz, Iran's Guards said they targeted US positions in Bahrain, and US-Iran talks remain stalled despite Qatari mediation.
why_it_matters: India imports most of its crude, so a Hormuz disruption feeds straight into oil prices, the rupee and inflation
Oil had been easing on supply-recovery expectations, which helped last week's rally
watch: Whether more tankers are hit or Iran's blockade-running convoy sails
Any restart of US-Iran talks through Qatar
questions: Is shipping through Hormuz being disrupted, or are these isolated strikes?
Does the 2027 timeline for US strikes still hold after the Bahrain attack?
conflicts: The 18:00 note cited one outbound tanker hit by a projectile plus a separate mine strike; the later note cites UKMTO reporting two tankers hit by projectiles, and says it is unclear whether Iran's mine-strike tanker is one of them
The 18:00 note described Iran attacking US bases in Bahrain; the later note says Bahrain accuses Iran of hitting an industrial site, while Iran's Guards say they targeted US positions
